requirements_summary:
Primary interest: Redwood Private (on-prem). Secondary: Dedicated (only if we can meet “no data egress” and residency controls).

On-prem constraints:
- Must run in Cedarstone-managed data centers (2x sites) behind their firewall; outbound internet access is tightly controlled/likely blocked.
- Preference for an “appliance-like” install (their words), with explicit upgrade path and rollback.

Integration questions (key):
- Networking: required inbound/outbound ports, support for HTTP proxy, and whether any control plane components require external connectivity.
- TLS: support for mTLS, integration with private PKI, cert rotation procedure, and whether client cert auth can be enforced at the gateway.
- Logging/Audit: audit log fields (who/what/when), export formats (JSON), destinations (Splunk/Elastic/SIEM), and delivery modes (push vs pull, syslog vs webhook vs S3-like sink).
- Identity: SAML SSO for Console, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC model and least-privilege controls.
- Retention: configurable request/response retention (or “no storage”) and ability to set environment-specific policies.

Workloads discussed:
- Clinical-style summarization and internal knowledge search; Cedarstone is cautious about anything that touches PHI directly in a first pilot.
- Latency sensitivity: moderate (interactive clinician tooling), but reliability + auditability are the gating factors.

Success criteria (draft):
- Demonstrate deployable on-prem topology + security controls in writing; complete their security intake with evidence references.
- Run a limited benchmark on de-identified data and meet target latency/throughput in their environment (TBD after deep dive).
notes:
Account context:
- Large healthcare provider w/ centralized infra/security. Team is actively evaluating LLM inference options but has a hard “run it in our environment” posture.
- Champion so far appears to be Infrastructure Platform (Director-level); security team is driving gating questions.

What they care about (verbatim/paraphrased):
- “No patient data leaves our environment.”
- “We need to know exactly what’s logged and where it goes—our SIEM team will ask day 1.”
- “Our PKI is internal; we can’t use public certs for internal services.”

Positioning notes:
- Lead with: deployment flexibility (on-prem) + operational controls (audit logs, RBAC, retention) + predictable performance.
- Avoid over-claiming on healthcare compliance language. Keep it to controls/evidence; do not use ‘HIPAA-certified’ phrasing.

Open questions to resolve in the deep dive:
- On-prem packaging: installer/upgrade story, offline artifact distribution, and support model.
- Multi-site: whether they expect active-active across sites or are fine with DR/failover.
- Audit logs: confirm exact fields they need (actor identity, request IDs, model version, policy actions, admin changes) and required export transport.

Internal next actions:
- Colin to draft a “ports/protocols + TLS termination options” summary for pre-read.
- Naomi Feldman team to confirm approved language for retention and audit log export claims for on-prem.
- Avery to align on who from Cedarstone attends (security + SIEM + network) to avoid repeating discovery.

Deal notes:
- Budget exists in FY if they can justify replacing a planned self-hosted vLLM build; they will compare support burden and auditability.
- Procurement will want DPA/SLA early; expect security questionnaire before any pilot resources are approved.
